en.name: Ephrem the Syrian
en.summary: Fourth-century Syriac deacon and Doctor of the Church known as the "Harp of the Holy Spirit" for his vast body of theological hymns.
en.body: Ephrem served as a deacon in Nisibis and later Edessa, in present-day Turkey and Syria, and chose never to be ordained a priest, dedicating his life instead to teaching and an enormous output of theological writing composed largely in verse, since hymns and poetry were, in his Syriac-speaking context, the primary vehicle for popular religious instruction and could be sung by ordinary congregations rather than read by scholars alone. His hymns addressed the full sweep of Christian doctrine, the nature of Christ, the Church, paradise, and the last things, defending orthodox teaching against the many rival theological currents of his region and era in memorable, singable form, earning him the title "Harp of the Holy Spirit" in Eastern Christian tradition. He also organized choirs of women to perform his hymns publicly, an unusual practice for the time. He died in 373 while ministering to plague victims in Edessa and was declared a Doctor of the Church in 1920.
